current_suggestion.pitch: Paul Bloom (Yale/UBC psychologist) covers the science of pleasure, suffering, empathy, and moral psychology with the same evidence-first rigor you get from Huberman or Attia but applied to questions about what actually makes a good life — territory your health and philosophy channels circle but rarely center. His work is a direct empirical counterweight to Stoic prescriptions: where Marcus Aurelius tells you what to do, Bloom asks what the data says about whether it works. Mostly solo essays and occasional interviews, typically 15–40 minutes, with genuine academic depth without academic inaccessibility.
